poem:
“The songs of the Portuguese
are like ships upon the sea.
They drift from soul to soul
and may so lightly founder.
Ah, the dish of sweet rice pudding
with cinnamon strewn over!
Ah, carried in by a white hand!
Ah, the hand that tended it!
Saudades – only the Portuguese
can feel them as they should.
That word belongs to them alone,
and they speak it true and good.”

ueberP1: Casa Dão Lafões is, without a doubt, a Portuguese house, even though it lies more than 2,000 km from Portugal. This regional restaurant is set in the picturesque Swiss village of Hägglingen (in the canton of Aargau) and was founded by Joaquim Sousa in 2003 to give the local Portuguese community a taste of home. To win over Portuguese emigrants through their stomachs, Joaquim Sousa counts on the help of his whole family. Together they prepare delicious dishes, rich in flavour and quality, that soothe the longing for suckling pig, kid goat and salt cod.
ueberP2: The dishes, and the atmosphere with “a Portuguese scent” – as the owner so aptly puts it – are created with authentic Portuguese products. Suckling pig, wines, cured sausages and even beer or soft drinks, straight from the regions of Portugal, accompany lively conversations about football, politics or the next village festa.
ueberP3a: The fine reputation of the food – above all the Bairrada-style roast suckling pig, the farmhouse stew, the salt cod “Dão Lafões” style, the roast kid goat with crushed roast potatoes, the suckling pig and pork fillet sandwiches and many other delicacies – draws Portuguese and non-Portuguese alike, the unknown and the famous. Football legend Eusébio, comedian Fernando Rocha, romantic singer Tony Carreira, as well as politicians and artists, have already graced the restaurant
